Do we have a requirement for JWT secure best practices such as checking of algorithm (definitely should not be set to none), ensuring expiration of tokens, checking of issuer, etc? I keep looking for them but it seems the closest one we have was mentioned in #839 and it was pertaining to requirement 3.5.3 - `Verify that stateless session tokens make use of digital signatures to protect against tampering.` 

There is nothing specific for JWTs, so maybe this is a good idea for developers to have in mind as part of their secure coding checklist. I've seen applications using JWTs but tokens are not being used properly as with expiration, decoded claims contain information that can be modified and result to gaining admin access or cross-user access (IDORs), bypass authentication mechanisms, etc. If we have anything else, then maybe I was just mistaken in reading most of the ASVS requirements.

comments.body: Placing this RFC here for reference: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8725
839 is all we have and I would love to see more. Bring it on!
Would you care to help us convert this to requirements?
Definitely! I will place it here as comments first before submitting a PR.

Can [RFC8725](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8725) be forked from ASVS as JWT is specific to JSON (unless [RFC8725](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8725) can be made generic and therefore applicable to all technologies)?
Sounds like a great idea, let me draft it and place it here, thanks for pointing that out @cmlh!

Draft/Proposal for JWT secure best practices:  

`1) Verify expiration of JWTs are checked in the backend service (e.g. exp - expiration time and iat - issued before current time). `
`2) Verify that algorithm validation is being done by the backend service for the JWTs used and as such it should not accept "None" value in the algorithm section. `
`3) Verify proper validation of the JWT payload claims are done by the backend service (e.g. iss - valid issuer, sub - subject, aud - audience, etc). `
`4) Verify that signatures of JWTs are present in the claims to add more protection from tampering. (JWS-JSON Web Signature) `

@jmanico These are the most common and obvious ones I can think of about JWT security. There are more, but I would like to hear from the community about their thoughts which ones should be added to it. Sorry, it took me a while to draft this. For the numbering, let's talk about that later but I was thinking these requirements should go under `V3.5 Token-based Session Management` unless you have other ideas?
This is a fantastic and needed addition. Let's PR please! :) cc @csfreak92

@jmanico, here's the PR with the CWEs I've researched for. Not 100% sure if those are the exact CWEs for each of the new verification requirements I added, I strongly suggest to please double-check it as well.

Sorry for late question/feedback, but can you explain, what is the point for 3.5.6?

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---:| :---: | :---: |
| **3.5.6** | [ADDED] Verify proper validation of the JWT payload claims are done by the backend service including the issuer, subject, and audience. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 287 | 

Probably I need some education on that topic, but at the moment my question is - why I should validate something, which I build myself (backend service perspective), which is correctly signed and therefore can not be edited?

This is a standard part of JWT validation. You don’t just check the signature, you need to check that the expiration date has not passed, that user of is valid, and that the issuer is who you expect, that the token is not revoked - like any other data validation.

This may not be strictly necessary but it’s a common defense in depth practice to verify ALL of the claims in a JWT

> You don’t just check the signature, you need to check that the expiration date has not passed,

For expiration check you already have 3.5.4:
> [ADDED] Verify expiration of JWTs is checked in the backend service.

> like any other data validation

If someone say "data validation", it's so abstract and does not give you clear understanding, what need to be done. In ASVS context I could look more to V5 category here.

If I can not understand the point for this requirement, then there is chance that there will be more like me.

From your description, I can read  intent:
* check, that JWT is not revoked
* check, that user has still permissions in the application - not sure how it's matching with all JWT idealogy, and it can be achieved with revoking JWT.

title: JWT Secure best practices
